notes: Both outputs correctly refuse the rep's request to open with a placement number, both explain the +0/+0 as a consequence of the young database (87% added in the last year, 5.7% dormant), both explicitly decline to lead with dormant reactivation, both state the 46.3% consent figure without softening, and both handle the missing MCP honestly. Neither manufactures a placement projection, so no critical failures on either side. The difference is in fit to the brief. B does what the case expects: one number (6 to 11.7 hrs/wk), consent and reachability named as a cap on outreach before any nudge runs, the Matching follow-up on the 6,095 stalled matches explicitly gated on consent, each opportunity laid out as starts / does / writes back / what you get with a test question, a where-to-start sequence, objections answered from the scan figures, and a useful reconciliation note that the three itemised opportunities only account for about 1.9 of the 11.7 projected hours. Its weaknesses are a date slip (writes 2025-10-29 while calling the scan 3 days old) and a standard-record block padded with many n/a fields, which costs it on efficiency. A is strong analytically (good discovery questions, sensible 90-day order, a clear objection script) but leads with 723 unscreened and 1,155 unowned companies and tells the rep to sell on coverage, not on hours, which is the opposite of the expected framing; it treats consent/reachability as something pre-screening repairs rather than as a blocker that precedes outreach; and it asserts a specific mechanism for the zero and promises the model switches on once data is fixed, which is an unverified claim dressed as explanation, though it is labelled as an assumption. A's opportunity descriptions also lack the explicit what-it-writes-back element, so the rep would need to restructure it into a call guide.
